sections.h2: Where is the Huron County Recorder, and what are the filing hours?
sections.html:
The Huron County Recorder is at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 100, in Norwalk, OH 44857, and is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Call 419-668-1916 or fax 419-663-4052. Document requests go by email to Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov.

The office states that anything submitted after 4:20 PM is recorded on the following business day, so the practical cutoff is ten minutes before closing. Under R.C. 317.13 the Recorder logs the date and precise time of presentation and records papers in order of arrival. Two documents for the same house are ranked by that clock.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Huron County?
sections.html:
The Recorder's page publishes a fee table effective January 1, 2025, and the first two pages cost $39.00. That figure rose from $34.00 when Senate Bill 94 allowed the $5.00 document preservation surcharge, and Huron County began charging it on the first day of 2025.

PagesRecording fee
1 to 2$39.00
3$47.00
5$63.00
7$79.00
10$103.00

Source: Huron County Recorder fee table, with rows trimmed for space. The page adds that each page after the second costs $8.00, each marginal reference costs $4.00, and the standardization guidelines still apply. A release that points back to a recorded mortgage is the usual source of a marginal reference.

sections.h2: Can I record a Huron County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. Huron County accepts most document types electronically, with two exceptions: plats and vacation documents must be mailed or delivered to the Norwalk office.

The Recorder lists six submitting vendors:

  • Corporation Service Company (CSC)
  • eRecording Partners Network (EPN)
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile
  • Hopdox
  • File And Go

Contact a vendor directly for its pricing and onboarding. Separately, the office runs an AlertMe tool that sends a notice when a document carrying a name you register is recorded or corrected, which helps an owner who wants to catch a surprise filing against the family home. The Public Access search site is the place to look up what has been recorded, and the Recorder asks you to email or call for copies.

sections.h2: What must a Huron County deed contain before the Auditor will transfer it?
sections.html:
Huron County's land conveyance standards, Chapter 14 of the Auditor and Engineer rules, require a deed to carry several items before the Auditor accepts it. The Tax Map Department works first come, first served, and combinations, splits, annexations and subdivisions can take several days.

  • the grantor's original signature, or a certified copy of a court order
  • a reference to the volume and page of the last recorded instrument in the chain of title
  • the grantee's complete tax mailing address
  • the grantor's and grantee's full names
  • the Auditor's parcel number and the property's site address
  • a completed DTE 100 conveyance form, or the exemption form if the transfer is exempt

The standards suggest a pre-transfer check at the Tax Map Department before signatures are gathered. The Auditor's office is at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 300, with phone (419) 668-4304, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

sections.h2: What does the Huron County DTE 100 form ask a seller to report?
sections.html:
The DTE 100 is the statement of value that goes to the Auditor with the deed. It lists the new mortgage amount, any balance assumed, cash paid, and the portion of the total paid for items other than real property. The conveyance fee is figured on what is left for the real property.

Two questions affect the buyer's tax bill. The form asks whether the seller has indicated the home gets the senior, disabled or surviving spouse homestead exemption, and whether it was in current agricultural use valuation. If the answer is yes, the Auditor requires form DTE 101 or DTE 102 as an attachment. A tenth item is an owner-occupancy application for the 2.5% reduction on qualified levies, and the form warns that leaving it blank blocks the reduction until another proper and timely application is filed.

The Auditor's receipt on the form covers the R.C. 319.54(G)(3) fee and, where it applies, the R.C. Chapter 322 fee. Ask the Auditor for the current rate.

sections.h2: Who can sign and witness a deed that goes to the Huron County Recorder?
sections.html:
A deed must be signed by the grantor, and R.C. 5301.01 says the signature is acknowledged before a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor. Most sellers simply use the notary at a title company or bank.

Once signed, the deed has to be recorded in the county where the land sits. R.C. 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later buyer who paid without knowing of it, which is why a closing agent files the deed the same day.

The Recorder is allowed to turn away a paper that is not required or authorized to be recorded, or that looks materially false or fraudulent. A person who is refused can ask the Huron County Court of Common Pleas to order the filing. The Recorder has no duty to inspect a deed for errors, so the preparer carries that job. Check the legal description, the spelling of each name and the notary block before anything is sent to Suite 100, because a deed returned for a defect loses its place in line.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Huron County itself?
sections.html:
Huron County sits in the Firelands, the western part of Connecticut's old Western Reserve, which explains why many townships carry Connecticut place names. The county was created in 1809 and organized in 1815, and Norwalk is the seat. It forms the Norwalk micropolitan area, part of the Cleveland-Akron-Canton combined area.

The Census Bureau puts July 2025 population at 58,250, down 0.5% from the April 2020 base. QuickFacts counts 25,763 housing units, a 74.0% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $166,000 and median gross rent of $848. Median household income is $67,878, and 7.9% of residents are Hispanic or Latino, the highest share among the four counties compared on that table.

The 23,490 households average 2.45 people each, and 88.4% have a broadband subscription, so online search and electronic filing reach most homes.

Wikipedia lists the Norwalk-Huron County Airport three nautical miles east of downtown Norwalk. The county covers 492 square miles of land and borders seven other Ohio counties, Erie to the north and Richland and Crawford to the south and southwest among them.

faqs.q: How much is the Huron County recording fee for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: $47.00, according to the Recorder's table effective January 1, 2025. The first two pages cost $39.00 and each added page costs $8.00, with $4.00 per marginal reference on top where one applies.

faqs.q: What time does the Huron County Recorder stop accepting deeds for same-day recording?
faqs.a: 4:20 PM. The office says documents submitted after that time are recorded on the next business day. The office itself is open until 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Can I view recorded Huron County documents from home?
faqs.a: The Recorder runs a Public Access search site, but its notice tells users to contact or visit the office for copies. Email Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov or call 419-668-1916 with the document request.

faqs.q: Do plats go through electronic recording in Huron County?
faqs.a: No. Plats and vacation documents are the two types excluded from electronic recording and must be mailed or delivered in person to the Norwalk office.

faqs.q: Who approves a Huron County legal description before a transfer?
faqs.a: The County Auditor and the County Engineer decide whether a description meets the Land Conveyance Standards, under R.C. 315.251 and 319.203. They may reject a description that does not conform and are expected to try to resolve technical problems informally with the presenter.
